answer:
Given system of linear equations:
1) $2x + 3y + 4z = 11$
2) $x + 3y + 7z = 15$
3) $3x + 11y + 13z = 25$

Write the augmented matrix $[A:B]$:
$$\left[\begin{array}{ccc:c} 2 & 3 & 4 & 11 \\ 1 & 3 & 7 & 15 \\ 3 & 11 & 13 & 25 \end{array}\right]$$

Apply elementary row operations to reduce it to row-echelon form:
Interchange $R_1$ and $R_2$:
$$\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc:c} 1 & 3 & 7 & 15 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 11 \\ 3 & 11 & 13 & 25 \end{array}\right]$$

Perform $R_2 \to R_2 - 2R_1$ and $R_3 \to R_3 - 3R_1$:
$$\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc:c} 1 & 3 & 7 & 15 \\ 0 & -3 & -10 & -19 \\ 0 & 2 & -8 & -20 \end{array}\right]$$

Perform $R_3 \to R_3 + \frac{2}{3}R_2$:
$$\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc:c} 1 & 3 & 7 & 15 \\ 0 & -3 & -10 & -19 \\ 0 & 0 & -44/3 & -128/3 \end{array}\right]$$

Since $\text{Rank}(A) = 3$ and $\text{Rank}(A:B) = 3$, which is equal to the number of unknowns ($n=3$), the system is **consistent and has a unique solution**.

Back-substituting from the echelon form:
1) $-\frac{44}{3}z = -\frac{128}{3} \implies z = \frac{128}{44} = \frac{32}{11}$
2) $-3y - 10\left(\frac{32}{11}\right) = -19 \implies -3y = -19 + \frac{320}{11} = \frac{111}{11} \implies y = -\frac{37}{11}$
3) $x + 3\left(-\frac{37}{11}\right) + 7\left(\frac{32}{11}\right) = 15 \implies x - \frac{111}{11} + \frac{224}{11} = 15 \implies x + \frac{113}{11} = 15 \implies x = \frac{52}{11}$

**Solution:** $x = \frac{52}{11}, y = -\frac{37}{11}, z = \frac{32}{11}$
proTip: Always check rank of coefficient matrix and augmented matrix to determine consistency using the rank test.
